key_insight: SurgNavAR demonstrates a practical AR navigation framework that integrates patient/instrument localization, preoperative 3D image-to-patient alignment, and real-time visualization on optical see-through HMDs, enabling the HMD to function as a standalone surgical navigation system.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between isolated AR/vision components and a cohesive, real-time surgical navigation pipeline—addressing patient/instrument tracking, image registration, and intraoperative visualization on head-mounted displays.
method: Integrate multi-modal localization and tracking to locate patient and surgical instruments relative to the HMD
Register preoperative 3D imaging to the patient using alignment/calibration routines suitable for optical see-through displays
Render and update navigation overlays in real time on the HMD with considerations for latency, accuracy, and surgeon ergonomics
impact: Enables ML and CV practitioners to develop and benchmark models for sensor fusion, real-time registration, and low-latency rendering in a clinically relevant AR navigation stack, accelerating translation of AI methods into intraoperative guidance.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram showing HMD, tracking sensors, preoperative imaging, and processing pipeline
Before/after overlay image: patient anatomy vs. AR-aligned 3D imaging on the HMD
Latency vs. accuracy trade-off chart for real-time registration and tracking
UI mockup of surgeon’s view with instrument trajectories, target markers, and confidence indicators
paper_title: SurgNavAR: An Augmented Reality Surgical Navigation Framework for Optical See-Through Head Mounted Displays
paper_authors: Abdullah Thabit, Mohamed Benmahdjoub, Rafiuddin Jinabade, Hizirwan S. Salim, Marie-Lise C. van Veelen
